reason: This passage from Genesis 12 portrays Yahweh as actively initiating a covenant relationship with Abram (the patriarch of the Hebrew people) and making extensive blessing promises to him and his descendants. Yahweh promises to make Abram a great nation, to bless him, to make his name great, to make him a blessing, to bless those who bless him, and to ensure all families of the earth are blessed through his line. Yahweh also appears to Abram and promises him the land. This demonstrates divine benevolence and favor toward Abram and his progeny, not antagonism.
